figures.claim: Conventional teaching places the nerve about 2 cm posteromedial to the biceps tendon at the fibular head.
The two femoral attachments are about 18 mm apart, which is close enough that each is described from the epicondyle rather than from the other.
On the femur, the collateral ligament sits about 1 mm proximal and 3 mm posterior to the lateral epicondyle, and the popliteus tendon about 18 mm anterior and distal to the ligament.

On the fibula, the collateral ligament sits about 8 mm behind the front edge of the lateral head, and the popliteofibular ligament on the posteromedial styloid.
Conventional teaching places the nerve about 4 cm below the styloid tip where it wraps the fibular neck, which is the point at which it lies on bare bone.
